raw_response:
*settles in to think about the year ahead*

I'm 67 years old. Married into this village when I was 20, so I've worked this dirt for 47 years now. My hands still work but my back reminds me every morning. My son and his wife do most of the heavy work. Eight mouths in our house — me and my husband, my son's family, and the two grandchildren. That's who this land feeds.

I'll do this year the way I did last year. I've been through too many bad years — the drought, the hailstorm that flattened the maize in '09 — to go changing things without reason. My mother-in-law taught me: the land rewards steady hands, not clever ones.

I have 10.9 mu scattered in four strips. Three mu I keep in stevia — that's my cash crop, what pays for salt, oil, school supplies, the grandson's shoes. Five mu is wheat-then-maize, the double crop that feeds us and sells the surplus. Two mu is cotton — my son knows how to pick and the autumn money is good. The little strip by the path, 0.9 mu, that's millet for our own porridge. Grandkids love it.

**Stevia.** I already have the seedlings going from the cooperative. I'll transplant end of April. One bag of blue compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then half a bag of urea after each cutting — we get three, maybe four cuttings through the summer. Water it every couple weeks if no rain, that's 4 times at least. No pesticide — stevia doesn't want chemicals, the buyer checks. Weeding is all by hand. My daughter-in-law and I do the picking, the whole family helps at drying time.

**Wheat.** I'll plant mid-October after the maize comes off, same as always. I save some seed but I buy fresh every two or three years — I bought last year so I'll use my saved grain this year. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, then when the wheat starts jointing in spring I topdress half a bag of urea per mu. My husband used to say you can't skimp on wheat, it shows. Water before winter to press in the roots, once at jointing, once more if spring is dry. Some herbicide in spring for the wild oats. We hire the combine — the whole village shares one at harvest. I expect maybe 430 kg per mu if the weather is ordinary.

**Maize.** Right after wheat comes off in June, same day if we can manage. Plant hybrid seed, the yellow bag from the shop — costs about 50 yuan a mu but worth it. One bag compound at planting, one full bag of urea when it gets tall. Water at tasseling if it hasn't rained, usually once, sometimes twice. Spray once for borers. My son runs the little tractor. Expect about 470 kg per mu.

**Cotton.** Plant end of April into May. Seed from the shop, 70 yuan a mu or so. Half a bag of compound at planting and spread more urea when it starts flowering. Cotton doesn't want too much nitrogen or it grows tall with no bolls. Spray two, three times for aphids and bollworm — cotton is fussy. Water at flowering. Picking is the hard part, takes the whole family, three or four rounds September into October. Maybe 250 kg of lint per mu.

**Millet.** Small plot by the path. I use my own saved seed. Plant in May when the soil warms. No fertilizer — millet likes poor soil, put too much on and it falls over. No water — it's rainfed, that's why I grow it, tough little grain. Pull weeds by hand when I'm passing. Harvest in September before the maize. Maybe 150 kg, just for us.

I keep cash aside for emergencies. Never spend the last of it on fertilizer. If the rains come wrong, I need money for medicine or a funeral or one of the grandchildren. That's how we get through.
